observations: Title and ending have a coherent teal/amber industrial identity. Rain, wet lighting and the large relay create a recognizable setting; menus are substantially more polished than the simple block-shaped enemies and rifle.

Clear objective markers, distances, named world signs and paused map made both archive routes learnable. Walls and low cover still caused several navigation collisions, but visible service/south-intake guidance helped recover.

Optic targeting produced satisfying visible critical eliminations, while moving interceptors were harder to track with stepwise inputs. The HUD exposes useful health, shield, ammo, cooldown and charging-threat information.

Receiver interaction communicated MOVE CLOSER and STEP INSIDE THE FLOOR RING after failed E holds. The initial ring/approach was not precise enough for me to judge range consistently from screenshots; short corrections worked.

Extraction had clear edge distance, near-edge and upload percentage feedback. Standing exposed rapidly cost health in attempt 1; moving behind the deck panel helped complete the finale. Attempt 2 completed with fewer kills by prioritizing travel and cover.

Restored records gave the three recovered people a concise narrative payoff. Several small monospaced labels, side hints and threat readouts are hard to read against the busy scene at this screenshot size.

No page errors appeared in successful driver responses. Three menu adapter input errors occurred between attempts: ambiguous RETURN selector, ambiguous data-close selector, then Deploy Again blocked by the still-open records dialog. These were reviewer selector mistakes, preserved in logs; aria-label Close archive resolved them.

gameplay.rationale: Compact objective loop supports alternate routes, optic combat, movement and cover; the upload finale punished exposure. Both wins were possible with few kills, so pressure may be permissive. Pause-assisted inputs limit difficulty judgment.
gameplay.coverage: Two complete wins, all receivers and finale; no death or successful charge-break observed.

presentation.rationale: Strong title/end typography, wet industrial palette and relay landmark; simple geometric weapon, enemies and repeated structures keep the scene visibly at vertical-slice level.
presentation.coverage: Title, handbook, records, first-person areas and victory screens; visual only.

usability.rationale: Controls, map, distances, recovery correction and extraction edge feedback supported completion. Reach/ring estimation and navigation around solid cover needed repeated correction.
usability.coverage: Handbook, map, pause/resume, recovery, reload and upload. Settings untouched.

readability.rationale: Major objectives, vitals and archive signs read clearly; small hints and threat cues compete with geometry, rain and multiple labels. Enemy optic precision required close observation.
readability.coverage: 1280x800 captures through two missions; no accessibility settings inspection.

aaaReadiness.rationale: A coherent playable slice with a complete loop and polished framing, but observed environment/enemy/weapon detail, short mission scope and limited encountered interaction variety do not establish broad AAA readiness.
aaaReadiness.coverage: Two complete ordinary attempts only; no audio, performance, extensive robustness or content-scale validation.

uncertainties: No hardware performance judgment from software-WebGL screenshots or capture timings.
Successful charge interruption, phase evade, death flow, extraction decay after leaving the deck, second capacitor and settings were not established.
Capacitor shot was followed by a spent cabinet and one elimination; precise damage attribution was not separately verified.
Synthetic frequent pauses and screenshot latency differ from continuous human input.
